clue.text: Football star, disheartened by the Spanish item in trattoria?

indicators.note: losing the heart, so the middle letter of the footballer's surname goes

parts.note: David Beckham, the England footballer
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A footballer, saddened by a Spanish dish, sits in an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes K, the middle letter, out of BECKHAM to leave BECHAM. The question mark flags that the definition is an example: the white sauce goes into lasagne.
explanation.definitionFit: White sauce is a staple of Italian cooking, layered in lasagne, so it is one thing you would find in a trattoria.

clue.text: Priest accesses stain, lifting cover of organ

indicators.note: accesses means gets into, so the priest goes inside the stain word
lifting means raising, which in a down entry reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: dye is a stain or colouring
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A cleric gets into the church to lift a stain from the organ's lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reads the stain upwards as EYD, and 'accesses' sets the priest within it. 'organ' suggests the church instrument, but it is the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyelid is the fold of skin that covers and protects the eye, an organ of sight.

clue.text: Lecturer resides beneath Sussex town dwelling

indicators.note: in a down entry, the lecturer living beneath the town sits after it

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, a county on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A lecturer lives in a south-coast town.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside town beside Brighton in Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovel is a small squalid house, a mean sort of dwelling.

clue.text: Extra flower stand for seaside resort

parts.note: more means extra, additional
a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Cam of Cambridge
to stand is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: An additional bloom on a flower stall at the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, the thing that flows: the Cam. MORECAMBE is a seaside town in Lancashire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a resort town on the Lancashire coast overlooking Morecambe Bay.

clue.text: Pithy Tory involved in false claim, endlessly

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the Tory goes within the other letters
false signals the letters of claim are not in their true order
endlessly drops the final letter of claim

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A short, sharp Tory gets caught up in a bogus claim that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CLAI, which 'false' turns into LAIC; 'involved in' then sets the Tory inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, terse and to the point, like the Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Work hard to become a clergyman in retreat

parts.note: to be is to become or exist

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the clergyman's title is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Someone toils so they can be ordained after time spent on a religious retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns REV into VER, giving BE + A + VER.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is an idiom for toiling busily and diligently, like the industrious animal.

clue.text: Flexible Friend, half used in past

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the half goes within the word for past

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by

indicators.note: half points to the latter part of the word Friend

explanation.surface: The Flexible Friend was a slogan for a credit card in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps the second half of Friend, and 'used in' sets it within the word for past. The Flexible Friend was a famous British credit card advertising slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bendy describes something that bends easily, pliable and supple.

clue.text: Complaint from unionist bypassing Scargill? Definitely

indicators.note: bypassing means going round and leaving out, so the letter for unionist is removed

parts.note: Arthur Scargill, the miners' union leader
it is, said emphatically, means definitely

explanation.surface: A trade unionist voices a grievance about the miners' leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bypassing' removes U from ARTHUR to give ARTHR. Arthur Scargill led Britain's miners' union through the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is a medical complaint, a painful inflammation of the joints.

clue.text: Hand having no clubs, host obtains trick

indicators.note: obtains means gets hold of, so the trick goes inside the remaining letters
having no removes the letter for clubs from the host word

parts.note: an emcee, MC, is a master of ceremonies, a host
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a ploy is a trick or ruse

explanation.surface: A card player's hand lacks clubs, so the host takes the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' leaves EMEE, and 'obtains' sets the trick inside. 'Hand' and 'clubs' pull towards card games, but 'Hand' means a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a worker, as in farmhand or factory hand, someone employed.

clue.text: City garden, very concealed

indicators.note: concealed tells us the city sits hidden across the words garden and very

explanation.surface: A city garden is very well tucked away from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' marks the hidden word running across garDEN VERy.
explanation.definitionFit: Denver is the capital city of the US state of Colorado.

clue.text: Once fallen at the front, troops are permanently honoured here

definitions.text: Once fallen at the front, troops are permanently honoured here

indicators.note: fallen suggests the letters of once have tumbled into a new order
at the front points to the leading letters of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A war memorial where soldiers who died at the front are remembered for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen' rearranges ONCE into CENO; 'at the front' takes the first letters of troops, are, permanently, honoured: TAPH. The whole clue also describes the monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a memorial to the war dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, where the fallen are commemorated permanently.

clue.text: Possible reply to: Which scout is able to fetch water, using this?

definitions.text: Possible reply to: Which scout is able to fetch water, using this?

parts.words: Possible reply to: Which scout is able to fetch water, using this?
parts.note: split in two, the answer reads as a boy's name plus 'is able', answering which scout can fetch water, and whole it is the camping pot used to carry it

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which scout on camp can go and collect the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The reply names a scout called Billy who can; joined up, the words are the tin camping pot he would carry the water in.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal pot with a lid and handle, used outdoors for boiling or carrying water.

clue.text: Aromatic herb with fish brought about argument

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the fish's name is reversed

parts.note: the ray is a flat fish
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A cook adds a herb to a fish dish, which starts a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns RAY into YAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a strong-scented wild plant used as a herb in folk medicine and teas.

clue.text: From Euston, I'm commuting with 'Echo' somewhere around here?

indicators.note: commuting can mean exchanging or switching, so the letters swap places into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller commuting from Euston station with an Echo newspaper wonders where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commuting' signals the rearrangement. The counties ringing London supply many of the commuters who arrive at stations like Euston, so the question mark is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the ring of counties surrounding London, so it is literally an area round the capital where Euston stands.

clue.text: Buffoon halted motorbike on a 1 in 5

indicators.note: halted means stopped short, so the final letter of the motorbike goes

parts.note: the Harley-Davidson motorbike, a Harley
a quin, a quintuplet, is one of five born together

explanation.surface: A rider stopped their motorbike on a steep hill with a one-in-five gradient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halted' cuts HARLEY to HARLE. 'a 1 in 5' looks like a hill's gradient but means one of quintuplets.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked clown of the commedia dell'arte, a comic fool.

clue.text: Not as sunny (degree less) outside to study here in Cumbria

indicators.note: outside means the trimmed weather word wraps around the study word
less signals the letter for degree is taken away

parts.note: duller means less bright, not as sunny
swat, or swot, means to study hard

explanation.surface: A place in Cumbria where it is gloomier, so you stay outdoors to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' leaves ULLER, which 'outside' wraps round the study word. Cumbria is a county in north-west England holding the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullswater is one of the largest lakes in the Lake District, which is in Cumbria.

clue.text: Kebab attracts Jimmy, turning up red-faced

indicators.note: attracts means draws in, so the kebab word holds the other letters

parts.note: a shish kebab, shish for short

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: jimmy riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, a pee

explanation.surface: A man called Jimmy is drawn to a kebab and arrives looking embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives EEP from PEE; 'attracts' puts it in SHISH. Jimmy is British rhyming slang: Jimmy Riddle, piddle, a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sheepish is embarrassed and awkward, often blushing with shame.

clue.text: Cleaner all set to exercise like fitness guru

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner

indicators.note: exercising works the words all set about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: A cleaner is ready to work out in the manner of a famous fitness instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exercise' signals the rearrangement of all set. 'Cleaner' looks like a comparative adjective but is the charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Atlas was a famous bodybuilder whose mail-order muscle-building course was advertised for decades.

clue.text: Very observant, reviewing jazz singer precisely

indicators.note: reviewing hints at looking back, so the singer's name runs backwards

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer
yes, precisely! is an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed critic reviews a jazz singer with great precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' turns ELLA into ALLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all eyes means watching intently, noticing everything.

clue.text: Language unit rejected spreadsheet program, spurning college author

indicators.note: spurning means turning down, dropping the letter for college
rejected means sent back, so the program's name runs backwards

parts.note: Microsoft Excel is a spreadsheet program
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A writer rejects spreadsheet software and turns down a college place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns EXCEL into LECXE; 'spurning' drops C to leave LEXE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexeme is a basic unit of vocabulary in linguistics, a word with all its inflected forms.

clue.text: Northern Irish Olympian has little time between matches

indicators.note: between puts the time abbreviation in among the letters of the word for matches

parts.note: peers are equals, ones that match each other
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An athlete from Ulster has a short rest between competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places T inside PEERS. Mary Peters won pentathlon gold for Britain at the 1972 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Peters, from Belfast, won Olympic gold in the pentathlon in Munich in 1972.

clue.text: Bad-tempered detective disrupts TV company

indicators.note: disrupts means breaks into, so the detective goes inside the TV company

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite TV company
PI is a private investigator, a detective

explanation.surface: An irritable investigator causes trouble at a television firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupts' signals the container. Sky is a satellite broadcaster in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiky, of a person, means irritable and quick to take offence.

clue.text: Insignificant bird before nightfall inhabits Lakes

indicators.note: inhabits means lives inside, so bird and evening go within the two lakes

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, so two lakes give LL

indicators.note: before puts the bird ahead of the evening in the run of letters

parts.note: the owl is a bird
eve, evening, is when night falls

explanation.surface: An unremarkable bird flies around the Lake District in the dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhabits' sets the bird and the evening between two lake abbreviations; 'before' orders them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something low-level is minor or of low rank, hence of little importance.

clue.text: Pass, for example, is in French

parts.note: est is the French for is

explanation.surface: A French lesson where 'pass' is given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests a test or a ball, but here it is the body's sense of passing out of the system.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge waste from the body, to pass it.

clue.text: Non-expert accepts a day cut short by computing conflict

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the amateur's letters hold the rest

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement done by amateurs rather than experts

indicators.note: cut short means the day is abbreviated, losing its ending

parts.note: Sunday is a day of the week
IT, information technology, means computing

explanation.surface: An amateur takes a short day off, and a computer argument follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims the day to its usual abbreviation, and 'accepts' sets that plus computing inside the amateur's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Disunity is a lack of agreement or cohesion, a state of discord and conflict.

clue.text: Ancient territory that woman risked, when swapping borders

indicators.note: the outer letters, the borders, of the combined words trade places

parts.note: she refers to that woman
bet means risked, wagered

explanation.surface: A woman gambled on a far-off land, with the frontiers changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping borders' exchanges the first and last letters of SHEBET, the S and T, to give THEBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was an ancient city-state, both in Greece and in Egypt, ruling surrounding land.

clue.text: Style of knitwear Daniel Craig perhaps wears outside in city

indicators.note: wears means has on around him, so the attractive man is wrapped in the city's outer letters
outside picks the outer letters of the word city

parts.note: Daniel Craig, the Bond actor, is an example of a hunk, a handsome muscular man

explanation.surface: James Bond actor Daniel Craig wears a jumper while out in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes C and Y from city; 'wears' wraps them round HUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chunky describes thick, heavy knitwear made from bulky wool, as in a chunky sweater.

clue.text: Dog alongside queen consumes right drink

indicators.note: alongside places the queen's letters beside the dog
consumes means swallows up, so the dog breed takes in the abbreviation for right

parts.note: the spitz is a breed of dog
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: The queen's dog laps up a drink right beside her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' sets the right abbreviation inside the dog, and 'alongside' adds the queen after.
